# Phone VR gaze rig (TASKS S1)

**Owner:** P1 XR & Interaction · **Prefab:** `Assets/ASTRA/XR/Phone/GazeRig.prefab` (generated by **ASTRA → P1 → Build GazeRig prefab**) · **One-call installer:** `Astra.XR.Phone.GazeRig.AttachTo(camera, …)`

This rig is for an Android phone in the Irusu Ultra viewer. The trainee looks at a control (a reticle sits at the centre of view) and taps the screen or the headset button, which Cardboard delivers as a screen touch. The input is reported as `gaze` (CONTRACT v1.4 §3).

| Part | File | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Contract | `XR/Input/IGazeTarget.cs` | `IGazeTarget { TargetId; IsGazeEnabled; SetGazeHover(bool); ActivateFromGaze(); }`. Optional extras: `IGazeLocatable` (a 1.0 s locate dwell that works even with dwell-select off) and `IGazeLabel` (the hover label text). |
| Interactor | `GazeInteractor.cs` | Each frame it raycasts 3 m from the head. The **first** collider wins, so an occluder blocks what is behind it. Hover enter/exit fires only when the target changes. **Tap** (touch, Cardboard trigger, mouse click or Space) activates the target on press. **Dwell-select** fires after 1.5 s (configurable; on in L0, a Hub toggle elsewhere). **Long press ≥ 1 s** recenters yaw. A short tap on nothing raises `onEmptyTap`. |
| Reticle | `GazeReticleView.cs`, `Shaders/ReticleOverlay.shader` | A dot that sits on the hit point (or 1.5 m ahead) at a constant angular size. It grows into a ring on a hoverable target. A radial fill shows dwell progress (green) or recenter hold (amber). The control's label shows underneath. It is drawn with ZTest Always, so it is never clipped, and it never flashes. |
| Head pose | `PhoneHeadPose.cs` | Sources in order: XR head (Cardboard plugin), then **gyro magic window** (Input System `AttitudeSensor`, no package change), then right-drag mouse look in the editor. Only the head moves the camera. |
| Fallback stereo | `PhoneStereo.cs` | Split-screen left/right eye cameras (63 mm IPD) when no XR display is active on a phone. There is no lens-distortion correction. |
| Settings | `GazeSettings.cs` | Player-wide dwell-select toggle (PlayerPrefs). |
| UI buttons | `UI/Gaze/GazeButton.cs` | `IGazeTarget` for any UGUI `Button`: a BoxCollider sized to the RectTransform, hover drives the highlighted state, and activation invokes `onClick`. Every P1 button carries one. |
| XR controls | `XR/Interactables/ControlTarget.cs` | P1's own buttons, toggles, dials and levers also implement `IGazeTarget`. |

**Recenter:** a long press (or a pause-menu RECENTER button calling `GazeInteractor.Recenter()`) rotates the "Recenter Yaw" parent so the current view becomes forward. If a scene `IRecenterHandler` is assigned, it publishes the report. Otherwise the interactor raises one `recentered` / `system` / `gaze` report.

## How the factory should add the rig (hand-off to the Integration Lead)

1. In `AstraSceneBuilder.BuildCamera()`, keep the camera, then add:
   ```csharp
   var reticle = AssetDatabase.LoadAssetAtPath<Material>(Astra.XR.Phone.GazeRig.ReticleMaterialPath);
   Astra.XR.Phone.GazeRig.AttachTo(cam, reticle, _font, keepDesktopMouse: true);
   ```
2. `keepDesktopMouse: true` leaves `DesktopRig` in charge of mouse look and clicks in the editor and WebGL, so nothing double-activates. On the phone, touch, gyro and Cardboard drive the gaze rig.
3. Make `TestTarget` (later `LevelTarget`) implement `IGazeTarget`:
   - `IsGazeEnabled => isActiveAndEnabled && GetComponent<Collider>().enabled`
   - `SetGazeHover(on) => SetHover(on)`
   - `ActivateFromGaze() => Activate(InputModality.Gaze)`: pass the modality through `Activate` instead of the hard-coded `Simulator`.
4. Make `Kind.Panel` targets implement `IGazeLocatable`, returning `1f`, so locate steps work with a 1 s look (CONTRACT §3).
5. Optionally implement `IGazeLabel` with the control's label (e.g. `CABIN LIGHTS`). Without it, the reticle shows the `targetId` in caps without its type suffix.
6. Wire `GazeInteractor.onEmptyTap` to the pause menu, if one is placed.
7. Run **ASTRA → P1 → Rebuild P1 assets and Hub scene** once, so the reticle material and `GazeRig.prefab` exist.
8. A scene can use the prefab instead (camera at the seat eye, tagged `MainCamera`). Don't keep two MainCameras.

## Platform: Cardboard proposal (needs team-lead approval; no package changes yet)

Full proposal: [`.agents/evidence/cardboard-proposal.md`](../../../../.agents/evidence/cardboard-proposal.md).

The Google Cardboard XR Plugin quickstart lists **Unity 6000.0.23f1+**; its README says 6000.0.58f2+. Our 6000.3.28f1 is newer than both, but nobody has tested it on 6.3. Requirements:
- Android min API 26, target API 35;
- IL2CPP, ARM64, landscape left;
- GLES3 or Vulkan (with Vulkan, clear "Apply display rotation during rendering" and use ETC2);
- Optimized Frame Pacing off;
- Input System active input;
- custom main Gradle and Gradle properties templates.

URP isn't mentioned, so the eye rendering with `Mobile_RPAsset` must be verified on the phone.

Until the plugin is approved and verified, the **gyro magic-window fallback** above is the route: gaze, tap, dwell and recenter behave the same.

## Tests
`Tests/PlayMode/GazeInteractorTests.cs` covers:
- hover enter/exit fire once;
- dwell selects after the set time;
- a tap selects;
- an `IsGazeEnabled = false` target is ignored;
- nothing throws with no target;
- locate dwell at 1.0 s;
- a long press recenters with input `gaze`;
- a real `ButtonTarget` reports `gaze`;
- the label fallback.

These are editor PlayMode tests, not phone evidence. Recording fps and comfort on the Irusu is still to do.
